title: No fertility refund: speculative-decoding acceptance across 21 languages (data and code)
description:
Per-item speculative-decoding acceptance for two built-in self-drafters, Qwen3.5-9B with its MTP head and Gemma 4 E4B with its assistant, on 200 FLORES-200 devtest sentences in each of 21 languages, with the code that measures it exactly for greedy lossless speculation (K = 1..5).

Result: no fertility refund. Under decision rules stated by the author before the runs (not independently verifiable; one gate amendment followed the first run), every gate passed and both kill rules fired in both families on their point estimates. Acceptance does not rise with fertility: the partial Spearman ρ of AL at K=3 with the token ratio, controlling for competence, is −0.656 for Gemma and −0.033 for Qwen (language-bootstrap interval −0.53 to 0.52). Every other language has lower acceptance length than English, so the refund fraction is negative wherever it is defined. Qwen's half of the verdict rests on point estimates.

Why (exploratory). Other languages have more continuation tokens than English, which are easier to draft (+0.026 / +0.055 step-1 acceptance), but acceptance within each token tag is lower outside English (−0.195 / −0.426), in all 20 languages.

Not claimed: an externally verifiable preregistration; recorded provenance for run 2 (documented, not recorded in the run files); sampling, wall-clock latency or other drafters. See README.md.

FLORES-200 references: NLLB Team et al. (2022), arXiv:2207.04672, CC BY-SA 4.0. Licence: CC BY-SA 4.0; the code (code/, reproduce.sh) is additionally offered under the MIT License (LICENSE-CODE).
